notes: ORE V3 (regolith-labs/ore), a Steel-framework program (no Anchor IDL — seeds live in source). Singletons config/board/treasury are const-only; automation/miner bind `authority`, which is NOT always the tx signer — claimOre/claimSol seed miner by the SIGNER and assert miner.authority == signer, while deploy/checkpoint take a SEPARATE authority account and seed miner by IT. The claim flow is wired (plan_claim -> claimOre): 11 accounts, payout in ORE base units at ELEVEN decimals, recipient is the signer's ORE ATA which the PROGRAM creates if empty (no prelude needed), and treasury_tokens is the treasury PDA's ATA (a two-step derivation no surface expresses). Two live comprehension gaps, both measured: (1) claimOre carries an OPTIONAL `bps` arg in source (ClaimORE { bps: [u8;8] }; omitted data = 100%) that the shipped idl.json and Orquestra both declare as args:[] — /build returns data '04' even when bps is passed, so a partial-claim ask silently becomes a full claim; 6 of the last 7 real mainnet claimOre instructions carried that arg. (2) checkpoint — claim's precondition — takes 8 accounts on mainnet (193/193 sampled) including the separate `authority` + `automation`, but the surface declares 6. The `stake` account is CPI'd across a program boundary and belongs to the SEPARATE ore-stake program — its owner is stakecNP..., not ORE. Naming gotcha (wire-verified): this Orquestra project speaks camelCase account AND instruction names (claimOre, treasuryTokens, oreProgram) — unlike the pump/meteora projects' snake_case. Recipes cross-verified against regolith-labs/ore@master + real mainnet accounts.

seeds.name: round_id
seeds.reason: seed is board.round_id (deploy/reset) or miner.round_id (checkpoint) read from account data — not a free-choice argument

why.automation: the seed is an authority ARGUMENT, not the tx signer account: an automation bot signs for a different authority (the exact confusion upstream fixed in ore-cli PR #150); the Orquestra-synthesized IDL binds it to 'signer'
why.miner: authority-vs-signer is INSTRUCTION-DEPENDENT, and the surface states it as a single fact. deploy/checkpoint take a SEPARATE authority account and seed the miner by IT (the confusion upstream fixed in ore-cli PR #150); claimOre/claimSol seed by the SIGNER and additionally assert miner.authority == signer, so claiming for another authority is impossible rather than differently-derived.
why.round: geometry vs state: source recovers the shape (['round', id u64 LE]) but the id's VALUE is board.round_id / miner.round_id read from account data — not a free-choice argument, so it stays an honest resolver
why.stake: cross-program: the stake account is CPI'd into the SEPARATE ore-stake program (stakecNP...); the Orquestra-synthesized IDL derives it under ORE's own id — a plausible-but-wrong address
why.recipient: the claimer's ORE associated-token account. The live instruction surface reports pda: null for it AND drops the `address` the shipped idl.json carries for the mint, so an agent reading the surface alone can resolve neither. claim_ore creates it if empty (payer = signer), so it needs no prelude — source-verified.
why.treasury_tokens: the treasury PDA's OWN ORE ATA — a two-step derivation (treasury = PDA(['treasury'], ORE), then ATA(treasury, mint)) that no IDL/llms.txt surface expresses; the live surface reports pda: null.
